events.content: On another subject, which country did her brother Ansel emigrate to?
I do not know.
Random question, but what kind of car did she drive?
I do not know.
What was her favourite opening?
I do not know.
Something I've always wondered. What colour was the coat Edmund lent her the day they met?
I do not know what colour the coat was.
Who made the wedding dress?
The quilt was pieced from offcuts of her mother's dressmaking, including a square from her own wedding dress.
What year was he born?
I do not know.
Which city did she stay in?
I do not know.
So what was her actual first word?
I do not know.
By the way, which university did Mum study at?
I do not know.
Different question. What was the name of the school she went to?
I do not know.
So far they've only let me sweep and sand. Six weeks of sanding.
Tessaly started by sweeping the shop floor when Corwin Hale was her apprentice.
They're saying the lower town might flood if the surge comes in with the tide.
I remember a time when a storm surge flooded the lower town in January 1953. Tessaly was only eleven then.
He entered his honey in the county show this year and came nowhere, poor man.
It reminds me of when Tessaly's heather honey won second prize at the Dunmere fair in 1991. She always thought the winner had added sugar.
Dad's going into hospital next week for a new hip, and he's dreading the boredom.
I remember Tessaly had a hip replacement in 2015; she even rebound the ward's visitor book with thread from a nurse's sewing kit.
At least I got some knitting done on the way. I'm attempting my first jumper.
Tessaly knitted one fisherman's jumper each winter, always in undyed wool. She never followed a pattern and never made two alike.
Anyway, I'm in a panic. We fly on Friday and I can't find my passport anywhere.
Oh dear, that sounds stressful. Remember, when Tessaly lost her passport in Port Saverne in 1983, she spent the rest of the week visiting the consulate.
One nice thing, though. I've signed up for piano lessons, and the first one is on Monday.
Tessaly regretted never learning the piano. She actually bought a second-hand upright when she was fifty-five.
We haven't spoken in weeks, and I keep going to bed angry about it.
Tessaly always advised that you shouldn't go to bed arguing if you could resolve things over a cup of tea.
This Saturday I'm trying something with saffron for the first time.
Remember that saffron bun recipe? It came from your grandmother, Hester.
My friends want me to do a New Year's Day sea swim with them. I think they're mad.
Remember, Tessaly swam in the harbour every New Year's Day until she was seventy; she said the cold reset the year.
Did he ever make a clock for her?
For their twenty-fifth anniversary, Edmund built her a ship's clock in a walnut case. He even set it four minutes fast so she would never miss the ferry.
Did anyone work there with her?
I do not know.
What was the biggest job she ever took on?
I do not know.
Wasn't there a cat?
Yes, her last companion was a grey cat named Vellum. He used to sleep in the paper drawer.
Did her honey ever win anything?
Her heather honey won second prize at the Dunmere fair in 1991, though she maintained the winner had added sugar.
Where did they go afterwards, for the honeymoon?
For their honeymoon, they took the night train to Vessant and stayed five days.
Did he ever hurt himself as a child?
I do not know.
Did they have any pets out there?
I do not know.
Did she ever travel anywhere to study it?
Yes, she traveled to Japan in 1998. She studied suminagashi, or floating-ink marbling, there with a teacher named Hayato Mori.
Was there anything she regretted?
Yes, she regretted not speaking to her brother Ansel for two years after their father's funeral.
Oh, and where did her cat Vellum come from originally?
Vellum came from the lifeboat station, where Tessaly had been living under the slipway.
Completely different question: what was the name of the dog she had as a child?
I do not know.
By the way, what was Uncle Jory's first word?
Jory's first word was "boat," according to the memories.
Different topic: what year did she have her hip replaced?
I do not know.
On another note, did her honey ever win a prize at a fair?
Yes, her heather honey won second prize at the Dunmere fair in 1991.
Something else I've wondered: how many steps were there up the lighthouse at Carrow Point?
As a girl, Tessaly used to count the 112 steps to the lamp room every evening with her father, Wilmot.
Changing the subject, what was her bindery called?
She was apprenticed at the Marlowe & Finch bindery.
Unrelated, but who was the teacher she studied with in Japan?
In 1998 she travelled to Japan for three weeks to study suminagashi, floating-ink marbling, with a teacher named Hayato Mori.
Before I forget, what was the tune Grandpa Edmund loved? We want to play it at the reunion.
Edmund's favourite tune was The Larkspur Waltz. He even whistled it while working, and it was played at his funeral in 2011.
That reminds me, I need it for the family tree: what date did she and Edmund get married?
Tessaly and Edmund married on May 14, 1964, at St Brannoc chapel.
